To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Online mindfulness is an accessible, acceptable intervention to family carers and is feasible to deliver in a randomized controlled trial.
It is feasible to conduct a RCT of an online mindfulness intervention for family carers of children and adults with ID.

it is feasible to deliver an online mindfulness intervention with additional telephone guided peer support to carers of people who have intellectual disabilities, and that this may lead to improvements in mental health and wellbeing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, feasibility, and effectiveness of online mindfulness interventions for carers of children and adults with intellectual disabilities (IDs).

the development and evaluation of a novel online mindfulness stress reduction intervention for family carers of adults and children with intellectual disabilities (IDs) that is delivered with guided telephone support.
the mental health of carers of people living with intellectual disabilities.

this study has shown that a mindfulness based stress intervention can be successfully delivered to family carers via the internet, with or without guided telephone support and that this intervention is acceptable to family carers.
this study provides preliminary evidence that the online mindfulness stress intervention with telephone guided support may lead to small improvements over time, but further research is required.

it is feasible to deliver the intervention with the addition of telephone guided support, that it would be feasible to deliver a definitive RCT and that it would be beneficial to conduct such a trial.

online Mindfulness is a promising intervention for family carers of adults with intellectual disabilities, and that the addition of telephone guided support may improve the effectiveness of the intervention.
the addition of guided telephone peer mentor support to online mindfulness for carers of people living with intellectual disabilities is a promising approach.
